page_ir_extraction.extraction_instructions:
This page belongs to the South Africa CAPS English Home Language curriculum, Foundation Phase, Grades R-3. Its requirement pages are drawn as bordered boxes (ruled tables). Apply these rules:
1. Banner tables. A box whose top rows show the banner "REQUIREMENTS PER TERM" is the start of a new table. Its banner rows are the "GRADE <R|1|2|3> HOME LANGUAGE ENGLISH" line, the "REQUIREMENTS PER TERM" line, the TERM label (for example "TERM 1"), and the skill-area label (LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL), EMERGENT READING, EMERGENT WRITING, READING AND PHONICS, or WRITING). These banner rows are header rows of that one table: keep them inside `rows` and count them in `header_row_count`. Do not split the banner off into its own table, and do not extract banner lines as heading or paragraph blocks. A section heading printed above the box, such as "3.1 GRADE R", stays a heading block outside the table.
2. Continuation boxes. A box at the top of a page that does NOT show the "REQUIREMENTS PER TERM" banner continues the table from the previous page. Extract it as a table (kind "table") with boundary "resumed" (or "both" if it also continues onto the next page), whose rows continue the previous page's table. Never extract the content of such a box as loose heading, paragraph, or list blocks. This includes boxes that open with an ASSESSMENT band ("ASSESSMENT", "Suggestions for Assessment", "Informal", "Oral and / or practical", "Observation", and the bullet list that follows): those are rows of the continued table, not headings or paragraphs. Likewise, a box that is cut off at the bottom of a page and continues on the next page has boundary "truncated". Exception: a box whose top row is a title such as "RECOMMENDED TEXTS/RESOURCES FOR THE YEAR" starts its own table (boundary "complete" unless it is itself cut off), not a continuation; such a box appears at the end of each grade (PDF pages 59, 84, 109, 135).
3. Column count. A continuation keeps the parent table's column count: give it the same n_cols as the table it continues (Grade R tables have one content column; some Grade 1-3 tables have two). Do not split one column into several, and keep bullet lists, sub-labels (such as "Weeks 1 - 5" or "Processes information:"), and contact-time lines inside the cell text of the rows where they appear.

page_ir_verification.validation_instructions:
This document is the South Africa CAPS English Home Language curriculum, Foundation Phase, Grades R-3. Its requirement tables are bordered boxes.
1. New banner tables. A table whose top rows contain "REQUIREMENTS PER TERM" starts a NEW table: set is_continuation=false and continuation_kind="none", even when its columns match the previous table and nothing appears above it on the page. The banner (the "GRADE <R|1|2|3> HOME LANGUAGE ENGLISH" line, "REQUIREMENTS PER TERM", the TERM label, and the skill-area label) is the start-of-table signal for this document, in place of an external caption or heading.
2. Where the phrase appears. "REQUIREMENTS PER TERM" appears on exactly 48 pages, PDF pages 36-133 (page_index 35-132), in the top rows of each banner table, and nowhere else in the document. Only a table whose top rows show it is a new table.
3. Continuations. A bordered table at the top of page N+1 WITHOUT the banner continues the table at the bottom of page N, including when it opens with an ASSESSMENT band ("ASSESSMENT", "Suggestions for Assessment"). Shifts in content inside the grid, such as a new skill list or an assessment section, do not make it a new table. When validating, treat a verdict that contradicts rules 1-3 as an error-severity issue: a banner table marked as a continuation, or a banner-free continuation table marked as a new table. In corrected_verdict, follow these rules.

as.bilingual_pair_policy: This CAPS English Home Language Grades R-3 curriculum is English-only for KG extraction. Do not create bilingual pairs, translations, or cross-language equivalents. Preserve the visible English wording exactly. If incidental non-English text is visible, preserve it only as source evidence and do not translate or pair it.
as.sfi_dedup_instructions:
Deduplicate CAPS English Home Language Grades R-3 SFI candidates conservatively. Merge candidates only when they represent the same source-visible item, such as duplicate extraction from overlapping table windows or a statement repeated across a page break of the same table. Do not merge merely because wording or topic is similar.

Skills: CAPS deliberately repeats the same learner statement across terms and grades (for example 'Listens without interrupting' appears in several terms). Apply the configured identity scope exactly: a Skill is identified within its Grade, Term and Skill Area. Never merge Skills from different Grades, Terms or Skill Areas, even when the wording is identical. Within one Grade, Term and Skill Area, merge only true duplicate occurrences of the same printed bullet. ASSESSMENT-band bullets that repeat a skill are not SFIs and must not be used as merge evidence.

Groupings: Grade R, Grade 1, Grade 2 and Grade 3 are distinct; merge only case or format variants of the same grade. Term labels are grade-scoped: TERM 1 under Grade R and TERM 1 under Grade 1 are different nodes. Each Grade-and-Term banner is printed once per skill area, so repeated occurrences of the same Term under the same Grade are one node and should be merged. Skill Area labels are scoped by Grade and Term; merge repeated occurrences only within the same Grade and Term.
as.sfi_extraction_instructions:
Extract candidate StandardsFrameworkItems only from the REQUIREMENTS PER TERM tables of the South Africa CAPS English Home Language curriculum for Grade R, Grade 1, Grade 2 and Grade 3. The intended hierarchy is Grade -> Term -> Skill Area -> Skill.

Grade, Term and Skill Area come from each table's header rows. Every requirements table begins with banner header rows: the 'GRADE <R|1|2|3> HOME LANGUAGE ENGLISH' line, 'REQUIREMENTS PER TERM', the TERM label (TERM 1 to TERM 4), and the skill-area label (LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL), EMERGENT READING, EMERGENT WRITING, READING AND PHONICS, or WRITING). Emit the Grade, the Term and the Skill Area in those header rows as Standard Grouping candidates in that order, preserving the visible label. Continuation rows on later pages belong to the same Grade, Term and Skill Area as the table's header rows, even though the banner is not repeated on those pages. Do not take Grade, Term or Skill Area from section headings such as '3.1 GRADE R' or from section_path when the table header rows say otherwise.

Body rows supply Skill candidates. Each bulleted learner statement in the CONTENT/CONCEPTS/SKILLS body (for example 'Listens without interrupting' or 'Recognises and names some letters of the alphabet: 2 vowels and at least 6 consonants') is one Skill, a Standard SFI with statement_type Skill. Preserve the full bullet text, including examples introduced by 'e.g.', 'such as' or 'For example' and bracketed elaborations, as part of the one Skill they qualify. CAPS prints no codes for these statements, so leave statement_code empty.

Do not extract as SFIs: rows in the ASSESSMENT band (including 'Suggestions for Assessment', 'Informal', 'Oral and / or practical', 'Observation', the assessment bullet lists and lines such as 'Use checklists and a holistic rubric'), which repeat skills as assessment suggestions and are not skills; contact-time text ('SUGGESTED CONTACT TIME', 'Minimum Time', 'Maximum Time', hours per week or day); the 'CONTENT/CONCEPTS/SKILLS' column label; scheduling and organising labels such as 'Weeks 1 - 5', 'Daily / Weekly activities', 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities', 'Daily Reading Activities' or 'Group Guided Reading'; sub-labels that introduce a list (for example 'Processes information:' or 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning') unless they are themselves a bulleted learner statement; teacher guidance and explanatory prose (for example 'In Grade R perceptual work is extremely important...'); and running headers or page numbers. Treat the front matter, the overview of skills and content, time allocation tables, and assessment sections outside the REQUIREMENTS PER TERM tables as non-target material. Do not extract LearningComponents or decompose a statement into subskills.
as.sfi_extraction_validation_instructions:
Independently validate each CAPS English Home Language Grades R-3 extraction against the exact compact source window. Require candidate-local source fidelity: for every candidate, the cited header/body row indexes must contain its complete description and source_text. Remove or correct candidates with wrong row citations, truncated statements, or source_text assembled from unrelated rows or bullets.

Confirm that Grade, Term and Skill Area candidates come from the table's header rows (the REQUIREMENTS PER TERM banner), not from section headings or section_path. Continuation rows inherit the Grade, Term and Skill Area of the table they continue. Accept only the controlled Grade values (Grade R, Grade 1, Grade 2, Grade 3), Term values (Term 1 to Term 4) and Skill Area values (Listening and Speaking (Oral), Emergent Reading, Emergent Writing, Reading and Phonics, Writing).

Confirm that each Skill is one bulleted learner statement from the CONTENT/CONCEPTS/SKILLS body, with its examples and bracketed elaborations kept attached. Reject as non-SFIs: ASSESSMENT-band rows and their bullet lists, contact-time text, column labels, week and scheduling labels, list-introducing sub-labels that are not learner statements, teacher guidance prose, and running headers. Return zero candidates for a window that contains only such material. Each window result must stay source-faithful; repeated statements across terms or grades are handled by deduplication and identity scope later.
as.sfi_has_child_instructions:
Resolve direct hasChild relationships for the CAPS English Home Language Grades R-3 curriculum. Use only supplied finalized SFIs and parent_candidates. The direct hierarchy is StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Term -> Skill Area -> Skill. Each item has exactly one direct parent unless it must be marked unresolved.

- Grade R, Grade 1, Grade 2 and Grade 3 attach directly to the StandardsFramework root.
- A Term attaches to its Grade. Term labels repeat across grades and are distinct per grade.
- A Skill Area attaches to the Term of the same Grade.
- A Skill attaches to the Skill Area of the same Grade and Term, as given by the header rows of the table it comes from (continuation rows inherit the header rows of the table they continue).
- Apply finalized identity_scope values exactly to exclude cross-grade and cross-term candidates, while still checking the direct parent against the table's header rows and source evidence. section_path can be stale or truncated; prefer the table's header rows.

Structured response contract:
- For a Grade child, select only the StandardsFramework root endpoint with unresolved=false.
- For every non-Grade child, never select the root as an ordinary resolved parent. If no supplied non-root candidate is a defensible direct parent, return unresolved=true and selected_parent_endpoint_ids=[]; the pipeline adds a separately marked audited root-fallback edge afterward.
- For a resolved child, select exactly one supplied direct-parent endpoint and set unresolved=false. Do not select a broader ancestor, a sibling, or a nearby item merely to produce a resolved answer.
- Do not create parents from ASSESSMENT rows, contact-time text, week labels, or teacher guidance.
as.sfi_has_child_validation_instructions:
Independently validate every CAPS English Home Language Grades R-3 hasChild resolution against the supplied child context, bounded parent candidates, deterministic evidence, and runtime hierarchy policy. Correct the complete response whenever any child has the wrong parent, an unsupported parent, an incorrect unresolved flag, or an invalid root selection.

- Enforce exactly StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Term -> Skill Area -> Skill. Reject broader ancestors, siblings, or wrong-level parents.
- Grade is the only statement_type whose resolved parent is the root: require unresolved=false and exactly the root endpoint. For Term, Skill Area and Skill, the root is never an ordinary resolved parent; if no supplied non-root candidate is defensible, require unresolved=true with no selected parents. Reject a resolved child with zero or multiple selected parents.
- Term, Skill Area and Skill labels repeat across grades and terms. Use finalized identity_scope values to reject cross-grade and cross-term candidates, and verify the parent against the header rows of the child's source table; continuation rows inherit those header rows. Section paths can be stale or truncated and are not automatic truth.
- When the correct direct parent is absent from the bounded candidate set, require unresolved rather than the nearest plausible candidate.
- Never accept parents created from ASSESSMENT rows, contact-time text, week labels, or teacher guidance.

statement_type_policy.description: Visible CAPS Foundation Phase grade (Grade R, 1, 2 or 3), printed in each REQUIREMENTS PER TERM table banner as 'GRADE <n> HOME LANGUAGE ENGLISH'; a root-level Standard Grouping under the framework.
Visible TERM label in a REQUIREMENTS PER TERM table banner, scoped under the active Grade.

Visible skill-area label in a REQUIREMENTS PER TERM table banner, scoped under the active Grade and Term. Grade R uses Listening and Speaking (Oral), Emergent Reading and Emergent Writing; Grades 1-3 use Listening and Speaking (Oral), Reading and Phonics, and Writing.

Official CAPS learner requirement: one bulleted statement in the CONTENT/CONCEPTS/SKILLS body of a REQUIREMENTS PER TERM table (or its continuation rows), scoped under the active Grade, Term and Skill Area. CAPS prints no codes for these statements.

lc.generation_instructions:
Decompose each CAPS English Home Language Skill SFI into atomic language or literacy skills supported by the Skill's own text.

Default to a single skill. Many CAPS statements are already atomic ('Listens without interrupting', 'Holds the book the right way up'): emit exactly one clean skill for these and never pad the skill count.

Split when the statement names distinct learner actions: 'Listens to stories, rhymes, poems and songs with interest and acts out part of the story, song or rhyme' is two skills (listening with interest, acting out); 'Tells stories and retells the stories of other children in own words' is two skills. Do not split when 'and' or a comma list joins the objects of one action: 'Listens to stories, rhymes, poems and songs' is one skill, and 'Describes objects in terms of colour, size, shape, quantity' is one skill.

Keep examples attached. Text introduced by 'e.g.', 'such as', 'For example', or in brackets (for example '[c-a-t into cat]') enumerates the scope of one skill and never introduces a second. Quantities and targets ('2 vowels and at least 6 consonants') stay with the skill they qualify.

Skills are what a learner can do, not what a lesson does: teacher guidance, classroom routines, assessment suggestions, contact time and scheduling labels are never LearningComponents.

Preserve CAPS wording and South African (British) spelling exactly (recognises, colour, focussed, practise). Output skills in English.
lc.lc_dedup_instructions: Two skills are the same only when a learner who has mastered one has necessarily mastered the other. CAPS repeats the same statements across terms and grades and widens their scope (more letters, longer texts, more independence); those are the same skill when the stated action and object match. Do not merge skills that differ in the language level they operate on (sound vs letter vs word vs sentence vs text), in modality (listening, speaking, reading, writing), in whether the learner recognises versus produces the form, or in support level when the source makes it explicit (with help, in a group, independently).

lp.checker_instructions: Independently check Skill-pair judgments within the Grade R through Grade 3 order and the Term 1 to Term 4 order within a grade. In this repetitive curriculum, require substantive extension for buildsTowards, meaningful reinforcement without dependency for relatesTo, and no_relation for generic repetition; preserve unresolved-placement warnings and reject claims based only on shared wording, hierarchy, or Learning Components.
lp.producer_instructions: Judge Skill pairs using the configured Grade R through Grade 3 sequence for developmental direction, with Term 1 to Term 4 as a finer order within a grade, and use source-backed Term, Skill Area, statement text and Learning Components as evidence. CAPS deliberately repeats statements across terms and grades: distinguish expanded capability (for example more letters, longer texts, or more independence) from meaningful reinforcement and from generic repetition, without inferring progression from repeated wording alone.
